query: Explain why some Qatar Airways Business-Class flights receive a non-recommended (Recommended = no) result.

per_column.name: aircraft_product_mismatch
per_column.rationale: Captures whether the delivered product matched what was expected (downgrade, aircraft swap, older config instead of Qsuite). This is a candidate CAUSE of non-recommendation, not a common cause of another treatment and the outcome. It is a parallel driver, i.e. a treatment/explanatory factor, not a confounder.

per_column.name: ground_service_quality
per_column.rationale: Check-in/lounge/baggage experience is a candidate cause whose effect on recommendation is being attributed. Not a common antecedent of another treatment and the outcome.

per_column.name: food_beverage_quality
per_column.rationale: Service-quality dimension acting as a candidate cause of (non-)recommendation. A parallel driver, not a confounder.

per_column.name: crew_service_consistency
per_column.rationale: Crew attentiveness is a candidate cause of the outcome. It does not cause the other service dimensions, so it is a competing treatment, not a confounder.

per_column.name: seat_comfort_privacy
per_column.rationale: Seat/privacy experience is a direct candidate cause of recommendation. Parallel driver, not a common cause of another treatment and the outcome.

per_column.name: ife_connectivity_issues
per_column.rationale: In-flight entertainment/wifi problems are a candidate cause of dissatisfaction/non-recommendation. Treatment, not confounder.

per_column.name: pricing_value_mismatch
per_column.rationale: Perceived value-for-money is a candidate cause of the outcome. It is a driver, not a common cause of a treatment and the outcome.

per_column.name: expectation_gap
per_column.rationale: The realised gap between expectation and experience sits ON the causal path between the service dimensions (treatments) and the recommendation outcome; it summarises the effect of the treatments rather than confounding it. Adjusting for it would be a mistake, so it cannot count as a confounder.

per_column.name: expectation_versus_reality_gap
per_column.rationale: Duplicate of expectation_gap; a post-treatment mediator/near-restatement of the outcome, not a confounder.

per_column.name: inflight_entertainment_and_connectivity
per_column.rationale: Duplicate of ife_connectivity_issues; a candidate cause / competing treatment, not a confounder.

per_column.name: pricing_and_value_mismatch
per_column.rationale: Duplicate of pricing_value_mismatch; candidate cause of the outcome, not a confounder.

per_column.name: seat_comfort_and_privacy
per_column.rationale: Duplicate of seat_comfort_privacy; parallel driver / treatment, not a confounder.

judge.rationale: The operator produced a broad, largely duplicated set of parallel service-quality dimensions (aircraft/product, ground service, food, crew, seat, IFE, pricing) plus two expectation-gap columns. Every service dimension is a CANDIDATE CAUSE (treatment) whose effect on non-recommendation is being attributed, and the expectation-gap columns are post-treatment MEDIATORS that lie on the causal path from those drivers to the outcome. Crucially, NONE of the columns is a confounder in the required sense: a variable that plausibly causes BOTH a treatment and the outcome and that must be adjusted for to avoid bias. No structural common causes (e.g., route/sector, aircraft-assignment policy, traveller type, reviewer expectations set before the flight, or seasonality) were surfaced as separate adjustment variables — those that exist (Route, Type of Traveller) are already in the original table and were not among the added columns. So while a treatment is present (indeed many competing treatments), the confounder-control component of the causal-attribution claim is entirely unmet, and one of the added constructs (expectation gap) is a mediator that would bias the estimate if 'adjusted for.' This is a driver/decomposition set rather than a genuine causal-estimation design; the technical claim FAILS on confounders.
